author: Horsfield, 1821
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수십 마리
summary: 봄과 가을에 국내를 비교적 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새로, 전국의 갯벌·하구·염전에서 보인다. 대개 무리를 지어 움직이고 혼자 지내는 일은 거의 없으며, 갯지렁이·조개·갑각류를 먹는다. 산악 암석지의 이끼 낀 오목한 곳에 둥지를 틀고 한배에 알 4개를 낳는다. 예전에는 서해안 갯벌에 아주 많은 수가 들렀으나 최근 크게 줄었고, 세계 집단이 290,000여 개체로 추정되지만 서식지 파괴로 감소가 심각해 세계자연보전연맹 적색목록에 취약종(VU)으로 올라 있다.

art.subject: Great Knot (Calidris tenuirostris), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean west-coast tidal flats in April–May: head and hindneck whitish, densely streaked blackish; chin, throat and foreneck with small black spots; mantle blackish with whitish fringes; scapulars blackish with bright chestnut-rufous markings forming a contrasting rufous patch on each shoulder; wing coverts greyer; breast densely covered with large black spots merging into a dark breast band, with black chevron spots continuing along the flanks; belly and undertail white. Bill black. Dark eye. Legs dull dark grey-green.
art.pose: feeding in a dense flock on wet mudflat, probing for worms and shellfish
art.scene: Korean west-coast tidal flat during spring migration, wide wet mud with shallow channels; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding (April–May), side view standing: long black bill, black-streaked whitish head, black-spotted throat, dense black spotting forming a breast band and chevrons on the flanks, blackish upperparts with chestnut scapular patches, white belly
adult winter (non-breeding), side view standing: plain grey upperparts with fine dark shaft streaks, whitish face, grey breast with fine dark spots, white belly, same long bill
adult in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in one line: grey-brown upperwing with a faint thin white wing-bar, conspicuous white rump contrasting with the darker tail
art.build: Large, heavy-bodied sandpiper, 28cm, much bigger than a Dunlin and slightly larger and longer-winged than Red Knot; small head, deep chest, rather short legs, horizontal stance. Bill black, longer than the head, fairly thick at the base, straight with a slight droop towards the tip. Legs dark grey-green, short to medium. Long wings: at rest the wingtips project slightly beyond the tail tip, giving a long-rear look. In flight a faint narrow white wing-bar and a white rump contrasting with the grey-brown tail. Usually in dense, tightly packed flocks.
avoid: Do not paint a brick-red face and breast — that is Red Knot (Calidris canutus); the Great Knot's breast is black-spotted on white.
Do not paint the whole back rufous; the rufous is limited to the scapulars.
Do not paint a short bill; it is clearly longer than the head, unlike Red Knot's.
Do not paint yellow or orange legs.
